prediction.raw: 1. You were right to call out your girlfriend's behavior. She was being extremely rude and abusive to a 14-15 year old kid who was just trying to do his job, and her actions were unacceptable. The kid was a new hire and didn't deserve to be yelled at and cussed out, especially not in front of other customers. Your girlfriend's excuse that she was trying to "teach him not to fuck with me again" is not a valid reason for her behavior, and it's disturbing that she thinks it's okay to bully and intimidate someone who is just trying to do their job. You, on the other hand, handled the situation calmly and tried to de-escalate the situation. You told your girlfriend that you had it under control and tried to get her to leave the situation alone. When she continued to be rude and abusive, you told her that she needed to stop being a bitch and called her out on her behavior. It's not okay to use derogatory language, but in this case, it seems like you were trying to make a point and get your girlfriend to understand that her behavior was unacceptable. However, it's worth noting that using insults is not usually an effective way to communicate and can escalate conflicts. A more constructive approach might have been to explain to your girlfriend why her behavior was wrong and how it affected the kid and others around her.
